text:
mei: quick sync on Mariner13B int4 onboarding. hitting intermittent OOMs during long-gen jobs (>=4k context) on canary nodes. sharing notes here.
raj: saw the failures start after enabling aggressive prefetch for prefix caching. can you dump the alloc traces?
mei: paste snippet: ```[2025-09-02T09:12:04Z] CUDA OOM: alloc 850 MiB failed
  GPU 0 total=79.5 GiB used=50.9 GiB free=1.1 GiB
  context: allocate_kv_slot(2048) -> prefetch_token_batch
  runtime: allocator=jemalloc arenas=8```
olivia: free=1.1GiB + many small free ranges = fragmentation. did we try different arena configs?
mei: tried arena_max_unmapped_bytes=64MB and background_purge=true on canary, slight improvement but still hits at scale.
diego: two immediate actions: 1) lower default max_new_tokens from 1500 -> 768 for mariner-int4 canary; 2) enable micro-batching on route (split batch 8->4) until allocator fix. both low-risk.
raj: also test toggling compact_kv_on_eviction=true in runtime; that reclaimed ~6G in our Sirocco run.
olivia: interesting idea: switch allocator to tcmalloc on one node to compare fragmentation patterns. tcmalloc may coalesce better but can increase RSS. worth an A/B.
mei: launch plan:
- canary A: int4, max_new=768, batch_split=4, compact_kv_on_eviction=on
- canary B: int4, max_new=1024, batch_split=8, allocator=tcmalloc
- control: int8, max_new=1500, batch=8
Run 300 evals per config (mix of short and long summarization prompts).
diego: add synthetic stresscases: 6k token priming + 2k gen; also a churn test with 200 concurrent short requests.
raj: record jemalloc stats and /proc/pid/smaps after warmup for each run. push dumps to S3.
mei: dumps uploaded: s3://rwinf-dev/mariner13b/jemalloc/1752223333_canaryA.txt and 1752223333_canaryB.txt
runtime-bot: canary deploys started: mariner/int4-canary-A -> host-group mrn-canary-1; mariner/int4-canary-B -> mrn-canary-2; control -> mrn-control-1
olivia: early results (first 100 evals):
- canary A (compact_kv,768,split4): stable so far, p95 latency 420ms, avg GPU mem 48.3 GiB, 0 OOMs, rouge-L delta -0.8 on long prompts
- canary B (tcmalloc,1024,split8): occasional OOMs (3/100), p95 380ms, avg GPU mem 50.1 GiB, rouge-L -0.5
- control (int8): stable, p95 360ms, avg GPU mem 55.4 GiB, rouge-L -0.2
raj: takeaway: compact_kv looks promising latency tradeoff, tcmalloc reduced fragmentation in some runs but still unstable under heavy long-gen.
diego: cost/quality note: int8 gives best quality for long summaries but at ~10-12% more GPU memory and cost. Document a fallback preset.
mei: suggested preset name: mariner13b.int4-constrained -> {"max_new_tokens": "768", "micro_batch_split": "4", "compact_kv_on_eviction": "true", "jemalloc_bg_purge": "true"}
raj: tiny nit: JSON in text above is fine for humans but we also need the runtime config YAML in ops playbook. add it to PR.
olivia: also flag: evaluation bias. reducing max_new_tokens can make Rouge numbers look better because gens are shorter. ensure we compare matched-length outputs when assessing quantization impact.
mei: opened PR #PR-1405 to change canary defaults and add preset. Ops runbook draft in GDrive: link (shared internally).
diego: ops safeguard: route-level policy: if OOM rate > 0.3% in 5m -> divert new traffic to int8 control for 10m and notify oncall.
runtime-bot: healthcheck mrn-canary-1: p99 1.1s, OOMs last 30m: 0; mrn-canary-2: p99 1.05s, OOMs last 30m: 2
raj: file infra ticket INF-3470 for allocator/slot-compaction research. tag @runtime-team. include jemalloc/tcmalloc dumps.
mei: followups:
- finish full 300-run matrix and post detailed mem/latency/quality CSVs
- merge PR to roll default preset to canary
- schedule allocator deep-dive next sprint (INF-3470)
- add perf-counter: kv_slots_allocated_per_request to telemetry (small task)
mei: thanks folks, will update when matrix completes. :shipit:
mei: (update) PR merged, canary at 7% traffic. monitoring dashboard added to Mariner13B entry.
runtime-bot: dashboard snapshot: mem drift +0.1GiB/hr, OOMs last 60m: 0, p99 latency 1.2s
diego: if stable for 24h, widen to 25% and then run cost/quality review.
mei: closing thread for now; action items in PR and INF-3470.
